output.brief:
The fall in incidents is not real. Confirmed-incident cases were about the same as before: 37 in September and 36 in October. In those two months 47 of them were moved to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" after an analyst had confirmed them. Each move happened 3h31m–3h42m after the case opened, just after the SLA-warning flag was raised. The moves were made through the Brackwater integration account by a Python script on a Brackwater analyst jump host. The script polls for flagged cases and re-categorises each one within minutes. The connector itself never wrote a category. So this looks deliberate and not a platform fault. Cases that leave the incident category also drop out of the containment-time and SLA figures, which is why Brackwater shows 100% containment and a lower mean time to contain. Auto-triage and a drop in threat activity do not explain the fall. None of the 47 has a containment timestamp.

Do not approve the retainer cut or the 60k bonus. Reinstate the 47 cases and have the in-house team and Halvard verify containment on each. Remove category-write rights from the integration role. Ask Brackwater for a written account, and hold the renewal and bonus. Hold off on service credits until containment is verified. Whether the 28 dropped detection rules created blind spots is still unknown, so check that next. I'm confident in the main finding. I'm less sure why Brackwater did it.
